prompts.label: Candy matched reference chroma v1 seed 1 / Qwen 2511 / Canny / 4-step
prompts.hypothesis: Changing only the seed may reduce reference semantic embedding while keeping the useful matched-reference chroma direction.
prompts.prompt: Recover an aligned RGB chroma donor for image1, a balanced but faded film source frame. Image1 is the authority for exact framing, borders, film damage, grain, softness, exposure, luma, geometry, character position, tree, leaves, background, suitcase, clothing boundaries, scratches, dirt, and all visible source detail. Image2 is a matched non-generated color reference for this same frame area; use image2 as chroma and colorimetry evidence for local hue relationships, saturation level, skin/hair/clothing colors, foliage, tree bark, background green, shadow color, and period film dye behavior. Do not use image2 as the luma, sharpness, texture, resolution, crop, border, grain, or geometry authority. Do not copy reference blur, compression, scale, edge placement, damage pattern, or any mismatched detail. Use image3 as source-derived Canny/control so recovered chroma boundaries stay attached to image1 source luma after inverse mapping. The output will be used only as generated CbCr composited over the original image1 Y channel, so preserve source alignment and make color sit inside the original light and shadows. Match the reference color families where they correspond to the same source regions, but keep uncertain or damaged regions conservative and source-bound. Avoid global tinting, yellow wash, magenta wash, cyan/green cast, oversaturation, monochrome collapse, invented objects, redesigned face, altered silhouette, relighting, sharpening, denoising, beautification, or reference-content takeover.
